title: Seminar · Translate a clause into a start time
question: If an implementation labels the second tray from minute 8 to minute 15, which clause would you show its author?
answer: P3 assigns a single labeler. Starting tray 2 at minute 8 overlaps tray 1’s labeling interval from 4 to 11. A citation to the seven-minute duration alone would miss the error.

title: Seminar · Keep the intermediate events in the tool output
question: Could a simulator that forces the scanner to wait for labeling of the preceding tray reproduce all three trace rows?
answer: No. Tray 2 begins scanning at minute 4, while tray 1 is being labeled. A program that serializes the entire two-station workflow would already disagree on the second tray.

title: Seminar · Run one intervention with the other inputs fixed
question: Why does cutting three scan times by two minutes move the final finish by only two minutes?
answer: The faster scanner lets the first tray reach labeling two minutes earlier. In both runs the labeler then works continuously through all three trays. Further scanning savings leave subsequent trays waiting for that station.

title: Independent task
question: For the same arrivals, compare two separate proposals: two-minute scans or three-minute labels. Predict the three label-finish times under each proposal before running the tool. Identify the first event where the traces differ from the historical run, then give a clause that explains the difference.
